prompt: Count the minutes two multi-day shifts share, but only the ones falling on a weekday between 09:00 and 17:00. Touching endpoints count as no overlap.
explanation: Two problems hide in one here, and solving them separately keeps the code short: the intersection of two intervals is simply the later start paired with the earlier end, and once that single interval exists the working-hours rule is a per-day clip. Walking the intersection day by day and clamping each day to its own 09:00-17:00 window means multi-day shifts, weekends and partial days all fall out of the same three lines. Using half-open intervals throughout -- comparing with isAfter rather than !isBefore -- is what makes touching endpoints contribute zero instead of a phantom minute.
hints: The intersection starts at the later of the two starts and ends at the earlier of the two ends; if that end is not after that start there is no overlap.
Loop a LocalDate from the intersection's first day while it is not after its last day, and use LocalDateTime.of(day, LocalTime.of(9, 0)) to build that day's window.
For each weekday take the later of (intersection start, 09:00) and the earlier of (intersection end, 17:00), and add Duration.between(...).toMinutes() only when the second is still after the first.
